newsitem.title: GERMANY: German steel alliance to cost 8,000 jobs-union.
newsitem.headline: German steel alliance to cost 8,000 jobs-union.

text.p: The planned alliance between German steel firms Krupp AG and Thyssen AG will cost as many as 8,000 jobs over four to five years, the IG Metall trade union said on Tuesday.
Harald Schartau, head of IG Metall's North Rhine Westphalia wing, told Reuters the union would undertake widespread industrial action to protest against the companies' plans.
Schartau said the companies planned to shut down a Krupp plant in Dortmund.
IG Metall would show "massive resistance" over the next four weeks, he said.
Krupp and Thyssen want to use this period to finalise plans for a joint steel venture.
The companies agreed on Monday to explore ways to cooperate. This rendered void Krupp's takeover bid for its rival which it launched last week.
